verdict.justification: Both deliverables follow all explicit formatting and slide-structure instructions accurately, but Deliverable B demonstrates much stronger project management acumen and deeper analysis of the underlying reference files. On Slide 4 (Progress Summary), Deliverable B incorporates the non-financial resource usage table from the other tabs of the INPUT 2 workbook (showing days used vs. planned by role, such as the Information Manager using "20 of 36 days"), which explains *why* the budget is currently overspent. Deliverable B also provides a more detailed financial breakdown on Slide 5 (breaking out individual material and travel cost lines against full project budgets rather than grouping them). Furthermore, Deliverable B catches a subtle scheduling conflict in the Project Log on Slide 7 ("Output 1 V2.0 goes to the assessor on 7 Nov, but Common Ground Bikes comments are not fully incorporated until 9 Nov") and turns it into an actionable question for the assessor on Slide 8. Finally, Deliverable A suffers from a minor temporal error on Slide 7 where it refers to the 3 November spend review in the past tense ("Review 2 was held 3 Nov") despite the report being dated 30 October.

decisive_issues.issue: Anachronistic past-tense reference to a November 3rd meeting in a report dated October 30th.
